summary: EC firmware mismatch after staged battery firmware deploy causes ACPI errors and intermittent boot/wake failures
description: Issue summary: After the automated battery firmware (FW) staged deployment from the depot on 2026-03-09, a subset of Dell laptops report ACPI/EC mismatches at boot and during suspend/resume. Impact: devices either fail to resume from S3 (hang on black screen) or boot into a degraded power state requiring power-cycle. This affects developer and engineering workstations and blocks provisioning queues for depot-managed machines. Environment: corporate depot (SCCM-like distribution), US-WEST distribution point, Windows 11 22H2 corporate image with Redwood baseline install tasks. Scope estimated ~0.5% of imaged fleet but concentrated on Dell Precision/XPS units.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Target laptop enrolled to depot and flagged for battery-FW update package (pkg id: BAT-FW-20260309).
2) Device downloads and stages update during maintenance window.
3) Reboot triggered to apply EC+battery FW.
4) Observe system fail to resume or boot; some show ACPI errors in early boot logs.
4b) Reproduced on a repro unit (Precision 5570) using same package and maintenance schedule.
observed_behavior:
- System stops at black screen during resume (S3) and requires hard power-cycle.
- Windows event logs show ACPI error entries and DEVICE_POWER_POLICY failures.
- Kernel / Windows early boot logs indicate EC (Embedded Controller) vendor mismatch and 'ACPI BIOS Error' messages.
- Docked devices sometimes report no battery and stay on AC even when unplugged.
expected_behavior: Battery firmware apply should result in normal resume/boot behavior; system should report correct battery and EC versions and re-establish charging / suspend-resume functionality.
logs:
Sample dmesg / event snippet from repro unit:
[    1.234567] ACPI Error: AE_NOT_FOUND, While evaluating a named object
[    1.234568] ACPI: EC: region 2 failed to validate (expected 0x34 got 0x31)
[    1.234569] ACPI: Embedded Control Interface probe failed
Windows Event Viewer: System
- EventID 41: Kernel-Power (unexpected shutdown)
- EventID 7045: Service Control Manager: failure applying battery driver
SCCM client logs: ContentDownloadManager.log shows package applied successfully but PostInstall step returns code 0xC000021A on some units.
investigation: Initial triage: Support confirmed repro using package BAT-FW-20260309 on two lab devices. Hardware team inspected a recovered unit and observed firmware metadata mismatch between battery controller and EC that suggests partial apply (battery FW succeeded but EC table not updated). Hypothesis: repository contained mixed firmware set (battery FW v2.4 matched to EC v1.3) and the update did not include atomic EC patch; some devices applied only battery agent resulting in version skew. Commands run: fwupd --show, pmset -g, SCCM content validation and checksum compare against DP. Verified that release artifact on central depot matched intended checklist but one distribution point (us-west-dp-3) had an older EC payload. We are checking DP distribution logs for failed replication window on 2026-03-08 night. Cross-team notes: hardware FW engineer (J. Park) suspects race between EC rewrite and battery controller update; imaging task sequence does reboot between steps but may not allow full EC commit window.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez (Support): Created ticket after first repro in lab and triage with hardware. Marking P1 due to developer disruption.
2026-03-11 - J. Park (Firmware Eng): Observed EC version mismatch on recovered device. Recommending immediate block of BAT-FW-20260309 distribution. Preparing hotfix bundle with EC atomic update.

2026-03-11 - Ethan Cole (Depot Ops): Paused package distribution on all DPs at 03:20 UTC. Confirmed us-west-dp-3 had stale payload (replication failed 2026-03-08 23:50) — reproducer found there. Rolling back DP payload to previous verified set.

2026-03-12 - S. Gupta (SRE): Added diagnostics to provisioning pipeline to validate EC/battery version post-FW apply; added gating check to image task sequence. Will coordinate with firmware team for staged rollout.
2026-03-12 - Ethan Cole (Depot Ops): Created hotfix package BAT-FW-20260312-ECFIX and queued for canary on 10 devices in IT lab. Monitoring scheduled for 24 hours.
2026-03-12 - Ava Martinez (Support): Updated impacted machine list and notified engineering managers of temporary workaround (do not apply pending updates to affected models).
resolution:
Workaround: Blocked BAT-FW-20260309 on all distribution points and instructed users to avoid manual updates until fix. For already-impacted machines, recovery steps: 1) Boot to Windows Recovery and power-cycle 3x to clear EC stuck state; 2) Re-image via USB/alternate DP if recovery fails; or 3) hardware reflash at depot if EC remains inconsistent.
Permanent fix: firmware team delivering BAT-FW-20260312-ECFIX which includes atomic EC+Battery update and version checks. Depot Ops will: 1) purge stale payloads from DPs, 2) add checksum+manifest verification step to DP replication, and 3) gate rollout to canary group of 100 devices across models before full release. Follow-ups: run a fleet-wide scan to identify devices with EC/battery version skew and schedule targeted repair appointments. Close criteria: 24h stable canary + no new repros from staged rollout + DP replication manifest validation automated.
next_steps:
1) Firmware team to publish hotfix and sign binaries (ETA 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC).
2) Depot Ops to perform controlled canary rollout and monitor telemetry for S3 resume failures.
3) Support to outreach to impacted employees with recovery options and schedule depot repairs where needed.
4) Postmortem document to be drafted if >50 devices impacted after rollout.
slo_considerations: This is internal support — standard SLAs apply; however, P1 and Sev2 warrant daily updates to stakeholders until stable. Notify IT leadership if ramp exceeds 24 hours.
notes_for_engineering: When reproducing, ensure DP replication timestamps are validated and run fwupd with verbose log to capture EC commit handshake. Consider adding a short wait-and-verify loop after EC rewrite in the imaging task sequence to guarantee commit before battery FW install.
